note:
Independent corroboration of all three reds — BASE_SHA differential in an identical tree and venv

Source: #2336 round 2 (a workflow_lint.py diff), which ran the affected tests
as part of its own gate and then re-ran the failures at its BASE_SHA
(`1040fff94a`) in the SAME worktree and the SAME venv. All three failures
reproduced identically at BASE_SHA, so they are pre-existing on `origin/main`
and not artifacts of that round's diff, of a dirty tree, or of environment
drift.

This is stronger evidence than the attribution check recorded when this task
was filed. That check established that each named commit exists, touches the
named file, and that the file is present on `origin/main` — consistent with
the reds being sibling-landed, but not a controlled comparison. The BASE_SHA
differential holds tree and interpreter fixed and varies only the commit, so
it isolates the cause.

Independently, the #2336 session also confirmed each failure directly against
`origin/main` (`93cee4593f`) by a standalone pytest run before filing. Three
observations now agree: direct run on trunk, attribution by commit/file
presence, and the BASE_SHA differential.

Failure count observed in the #2336 round-2 gate leg: 3 failed alongside
3,972 passed, i.e. the three named here and nothing else in that leg's scope.

One correction to carry forward, repeated from the filed body because it is
easy to lose: `test_workflow_lint_prod_import_lockfile::test_live_tree_clean`
is NOT #2474's alone. Its `== 7` dangling-root pin now sees 11, and the four
new roots split #2379 three ways (`issue2379_analysis`, `issue2379_capture`,
`issue2379_mapfit`) plus #2474 one (`issue2474_fit`). A fix touching only
#2474 leaves the assertion red at 10.

No action requested of #2336 — it is not the cause and is not blocked by
these; it routes around them by attributing them at every gate.
